State machine transitions

Source: R/state-machine.R
sim_transition.Rd

Helper to declare one transition of a "state_machine" block.

Usage

sim_transition(
  from,
  to,
  guard = "TRUE",
  after = 0,
  action = NULL,
  priority = NA
)

Arguments

from, to

State names.

guard

Guard expression (string) or function; "TRUE" by default.

after

Minimum time in from before the transition may fire.

action

Optional transition action.

priority

Optional priority; smaller values are tried first.

Value

A sim_transition object.

Details

A state machine block is a discrete block that executes at every sample hit of its clock (period, offset). At a hit it:

  1. collects the transitions leaving the current state, sorted by priority (smaller first) and then by their position in the list;

  2. takes the first transition whose guard holds and whose after time (time spent in the current state) has elapsed;

  3. runs the exit action of the old state, the transition action and the entry action of the new state, in that order, then records the entry time;

  4. when no transition fires, runs the during action of the current state.

The entry action of the initial state runs at the first sample hit, before transitions are considered, with the inputs and time of that hit.

At most one transition fires per sample hit, so evaluation never loops. Outputs are computed after the transition, which means the outputs at a hit depend on the inputs at the same hit (direct feedthrough).

Guards and actions are portable strings or R functions. A guard string is an expression in u (the input vector), t, elapsed (time in the current state), the data variables and the parameters of the enclosing model or subsystem. An action string assigns data variables, for example "count <- count + 1"; each data variable must still hold one finite number afterwards. A guard function has signature function(u, t, elapsed, data) and returns TRUE or FALSE; an action function has signature function(data, u, t) and returns the new data vector: either unnamed with one value per variable, in the order of data, or named with exactly the data variable names, in any order (values are matched by name). Guards and actions must be pure functions of their arguments, because the block evaluates them to compute its outputs and again to compute its next state.

after compares the time spent in the state, t - entry time, with the requested duration, allowing only for the rounding of that subtraction, so the behavior does not depend on where the time axis starts.

The block's parameters are states (character), initial (state name), transitions (a list of sim_transition()), entry, exit, during (named lists of actions by state), data (named numeric initial values of data variables), outputs (optional named list of numeric output vectors by state), n_inputs, period and offset. Output ports are state (index of the active state in states), then y when outputs is given, then data when there are data variables.

See also

sim_check_state_machine().

Examples

# A thermostat that heats below 19 degrees and stops above 21.
m <- sim_model("thermostat")
sim_add_block(m, "integrator", "temp", initial = 18)
sim_add_block(m, "state_machine", "ctrl", period = 0.1,
  states = c("heating", "idle"),
  transitions = list(
    sim_transition("heating", "idle", "u[1] > 21"),
    sim_transition("idle", "heating", "u[1] < 19")),
  outputs = list(heating = 1, idle = 0))
sim_add_block(m, "expression", "rate", expr = "2 * u[1] - 0.1 * (u[2] - 10)")
sim_add_block(m, "mux", "mx")
sim_connect(m, "temp", "ctrl")
sim_connect(m, "ctrl", "mx", output = "y", input = 1)
sim_connect(m, "temp", "mx", input = 2)
sim_connect(m, "mx", "rate")
sim_connect(m, "rate", "temp")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(m), c(0, 10))
range(sim_signal(r, "temp"))
#> [1] 18.00000 21.02953
